# Implementation Plan
 
-Status: draft (flow-init skill fills this after context and brainstorm)
+Status: implemented on `feat/telegram-remote-control-relay`; AC8 (live run) waits for the operator.
 
 ## Approach
 
-Chosen approach and why (link brainstorm alternatives if any).
+Keep the existing split: `keryx serve` owns Telegram, the shell is a client over `/v1/remote/*`. Each
+criterion is closed at the narrowest layer that already owns the behaviour, with a test beside it:
+
+- Mirror shell prompts through the bridge's `askApproval`/`askUser`, not through the TUI, so a turn typed in
+  the shell is covered too (`src/tui/approval-mirror.ts`). First answer wins; the loser is closed with
+  `prompt-close`.
+- Reminders live in `RemoteHttpSurface`, next to the prompt table, so the timer dies with the prompt.
+- Commands from the topic wait for an idle main in the command router (`awaitIdle`), with a notice, instead of
+  being refused.
+- Progress notes are composed from counts and names only (`src/remote/progress-notes.ts`), driven by the tool
+  hook and the subagent fleet listener, with one rate limiter.
+- A status question is answered by the bridge from session state, so it never reaches the model or the queue.
+- Close archives (`closeForumTopic`) instead of deleting; the orphan sweep does the same for a killed shell.
+
+Rejected: a timer-driven ticker for progress (notes would fire in an idle turn), and a model-written summary
+(slow, can leak tool output).
 
 ## Steps
 
-1. ...
+1. AC7 + AC1/AC2: archive on close, mirror approvals and `ask_user`, `prompt-close` for the loser. (a556a84a)
+2. AC3: reminders, 2 min, at most 3. (c9d17c57)
+3. AC4: `/route` on the menu, queue-when-busy for `/route`, `/external`, `/external-agents`, `/model`. (2121fcf5)
+4. AC5, AC6, AC7 explicit test: progress notes, instant status answers, topic survives exit and Ctrl+C. (f9f0ee34)
+5. AC9: README, drive-keryx-remotely guide (new "What the topic hears" and "What happens when the shell closes"),
+   cli-reference, wiki page, CHANGELOG; `mkdocs build --strict` passes.
+6. AC8: operator-run live review (not started; the operator runs it):
+   1. Install the branch build (`npm pack`, then `npm i -g` the tarball; npm only) and run `keryx update` in the
+      test project. Telegram connected via `/channels`; `keryx serve` running.
+   2. `/clear`, then in a shell start a long review (a real PR with several reviewers) and type `/remote-control`.
+   3. From now on touch only Telegram: answer every approval and `ask_user` from the topic; ask "how is it going?"
+      once mid-run; send `/model` or `/route` once while main is busy and check the queued notice.
+   4. Leave one prompt unanswered for over 2 minutes and check the reminder.
+   5. When the review ends, `/exit` in the shell and check the topic is archived with its history.
+   6. Export the topic's message log and attach it to the flow with the shell's transcript; then
+      `keryx flow ac confirm 419 AC8 --note "<log path>"`.
 
 ## Risks
 
-- ...
+- Progress notes fire on tool calls and subagent events only; a long silent model step produces no note.
+- A wave-start note names only the subagents known at that moment; the rate limit coalesces the rest.
+- Status questions are matched by a short phrase list (en/ru); anything else goes to the model when main is idle
+  and is queued as work when busy.
+- Everything was tested against a fake Bot API; real Telegram behaviour (closed topics, reactions) is AC8.

### Limits and orphans
 
-`orphanMs` (default 10 minutes): a session that stops heartbeating is announced in its topic, and the topic is deleted after the window; a heartbeat inside it cancels this. `runTimeoutMs` (default 30 minutes): a run started from Telegram is interrupted by the shell and the topic is told (`run-limits.ts`).

## [Unreleased]
 
+### Remote control
+
+- Every approval, `ask_user` question and queue dialog the shell raises is mirrored to the Telegram topic with buttons, also for a turn typed in the shell. The first answer wins from either side and closes the other exactly once (`prompt-close`).
+- An unanswered question gets a reminder in the topic every 2 minutes, at most 3 times.
+- `/route` is on the topic menu (`/route on|off` ask first). `/route`, `/external`, `/external-agents` and `/model` are queued with a notice while main is busy and run when it goes idle, instead of being refused. `/mode` takes effect at once.
+- Progress notes in the topic at subagent wave boundaries and after tool-heavy stretches, at most one a minute: counts, tool names and labels only, never tool output. A short status question ("how is it going?") is answered from session state while the turn runs.
+- Closing the shell archives the topic (closing note, topic and history stay readable) instead of deleting it; a killed shell is archived after the orphan window. Only channel Disconnect deletes topics.

+### What the topic hears
+
+While `/remote-control` is on, you can run a long job from your phone and not lose
+track of it. Nothing below needs a setting; the intervals are fixed.
+
+**Every question the shell raises is posted.** A command approval, an `ask_user`
+question and a queue dialog all appear in the topic with Allow / Deny or one button
+per option, **whether the turn started in the shell or in the topic**. The first
+answer wins and the other side is closed exactly once:
+
+- Answer in the topic first: the shell's dock closes the same question and carries on
+  with your answer; the message is edited to say who answered and when.
+- Answer in the terminal first: the Telegram message is edited to "answered in the
+  shell" and its buttons stop working, so a late press does nothing.
+
+**Reminders.** A question nobody has answered gets a reminder in the topic every
+2 minutes, at most 3 times. The reminder quotes the first line of what was asked (cut at 80 characters), says
+when the question expires and points at the buttons on the original message; it adds
+no new buttons. A question that is answered, expired or closed stops its reminders.
+
+**Progress notes.** During a turn the topic gets a short note at a wave boundary (the
+first subagent of a review fan-out starting, and the last one finishing) and after a
+tool-heavy stretch (8 tool calls since the last note). At most **one note a minute**
+goes out; if a second one is due earlier, the weightier one is held and sent when the
+minute ends, and any note still held when the turn ends is dropped. A note carries
+counts, tool names and subagent labels only, for example `Still working: 12 tool calls
+in the last 1m (read_file, shell_exec). 3m 20s into this turn.` Tool input, tool output
+and the model's text never go into a note.
+
+**Status questions are answered at once.** While a turn runs, a short plain line that
+only asks how it is going (`status`, `how is it going?`, `are you still working?`,
+`статус`, `как дела?`) is answered from the shell's own state without waiting for the
+turn: elapsed time, tool calls so far and the last tool, subagents still running, how
+many messages wait, how many questions wait for you, and the mode. It is not queued
+and does not reach the model. A longer message that merely contains the word "status"
+is work and is queued as usual, and when the shell is idle the same words go to the
+model like any other line.
+
+### What happens when the shell closes
+
+The topic is **archived, not deleted**. When the shell exits (`/exit`, `/quit`), the
+topic gets a closing note ("This topic is archived: the history stays here and nothing
+more will be posted") and is closed. It stays in the group, readable, with everything that was said in it.
+When the shell is killed (Ctrl+C twice, a closed terminal, a crash) it cannot say
+goodbye: `serve` announces the silence in the topic and, after the orphan window
+(10 minutes by default), posts the same note and archives it. A heartbeat inside the
+window cancels that. A resumed session (`keryx shell --continue`) gets a new topic;
+`/history` copies the last messages into it. Only **Disconnect** in `/channels` deletes
+topics.
